newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot electricity prices move higher.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot electricity prices move higher.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. mostly moved higher Wednesday with expectations spot prices would jump on Thursday ahead of forecasts of frigid weekend temperatures.
Forecasts called for temperatures to drop Thursday to 15 to 25 degrees Fahrenheit below normal and continue there through the weekend through much of the Mid-West.
"Prices could get considerably higher tomorrow for Friday business, the forecasts are calling for record cold," said one ECAR trader.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday were steady to higher at $27.00-29.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $26.00-29.00 on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were assessed steady at $15.00-18.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was said to have held steady at $23.50-24.00.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), where temperatures continued to be extremely cold, peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were discussed higher at $38.00-39.50 from $36.00-39.00 on Tuesday.
Off-peak next day non-firm MAPP power was talked higher at $15.00-19.00 from $14.00-18.00 on Tuesday.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday were talked higher at $27.00-29.00 from $26.00-28.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
MAIN off peak next day power was also said to have risen to $17.00-19.00 from $16.00-18.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were talked lower at $27.00-31.00 from $30.00-34.00 on Tuesday for Wednesday delivery, the sources said.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP held steady at $17.00-19.00 per MWh.
February SPP was said to have risen to $24.00-24.25 from $23.85-24.25 on Tuesday, the sources said.
One source quoted March SPP at $22.90-23.20, while April was quoted at $18.00-18.50 and July/August at $27.75-28.25 per MWh.
Separately, Consumers Energy's 780 MW Palisades nuclear power plant in South Haven, Mich., was boosting electricity production Wednesday after a shutdown for repairs to main steam isolation valves.
IES Utilities has said it expects its 538 MW Duane Arnold nuclear power plant in Palo, Iowa to resume electricity production Thursday following a repair shutdown over the weekend.
Also, Duquesne Light Co said the 833 megawatt (MW) Beaver Valley nuclear power unit 2 in Shippingport, Pa., resumed electricity output Wednesday afternoon following a shutdown for repairs.
